en: The Yoga of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra, Chapter One:
Also known as the Ritual for the Five-Syllable Mantra.
By Kai-fu Yi-tong San-si Te-jin Shi Hong-lu Qing.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, who was the Duke of Sù with a fief of three thousand households, invested with purple robes, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and titled Dàjiàn (Great Mirror), bearing the epithet Dàguǎngzhì (Great Universal Wisdom). At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī...
In the great assembly of Vairocana,
he rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!”
I shall now proclaim the original five-syllable dhāraṇī.
If there are good sons or good daughters who recite it even once,
[they shall obtain such benefits].
The merit of reading, reciting, receiving, and upholding the Sūtra-piṭaka of the Dharma teachings expounded by all Tathāgatas—
Vairocana Buddha [is that].
He addressed Mañjuśrī, saying,
"Speak as you wish.
Thereupon, Mañjuśrī spoke.
The Vidyā says:
"A-ra-pa-ca-na. As soon as this dhāraṇī was spoken, all the teachings expounded by the Tathāgatas [were established].
These are subsumed within the five-syllable dhāraṇī,
which enables sentient beings to achieve the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
I shall now explain the maṇḍala ritual.
On either the fourteenth or fifteenth day,
one should select an extremely pure location and construct a maṇḍala,
smearing the ground with cow dung (gomaya).
Furthermore, one should smear it with white sandalwood paste,
making it as large or small as desired within the maṇḍala.
One should depict Mañjuśrī in the form of a five-crested youth,
his body the color of *uragasāra* gold,
adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments.
Holding a vajra sword in the right hand and a Dharma volume in the left hand,
he sits within a moon disc;
at the four sides of the moon disc—
The ācārya performs the ritual circumambulation while reciting the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī; facing this maṇḍala,
he binds the vajra-sword mudrā and performs the recitation.
At that time, Mañjuśrī empowered this ācārya,
whereby he immediately attained unimpeded eloquence;
Mañjuśrī then manifested his physical form before him.
Having explained each of the profound meanings and principles of this dhāraṇī,
the ācārya should then prostrate and exit the maṇḍala to confer the bodhisattva precepts upon the disciple.
He then covered the disciple’s eyes with crimson silk and led him into the entrance of the maṇḍala, where he stood.
At that time, the ācārya addressed the disciple, saying:
"You have now obtained the Prajñāpāramitā of all Tathāgatas.
From this day forward, you must not speak of this vidyā to others;
do not cause your samaya-dharma to be broken."
This dhāraṇī is to be kept strictly secret.
*Arapacanā* means "the fulfillment of all wishes."
Why is this? The syllable *A* signifies the aspiration for bodhi;
the syllable *Ra* signifies deep attachment to and non-abandonment of sentient beings.
The syllable *pa* signifies the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*).
The syllable *ca* signifies sublime conduct (*sucarita*).
The syllable *na* signifies the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*).
They aspire to enlightenment and do not abandon sentient beings;
they enter deeply into the practice of the ultimate truth (paramārthasatya) and cultivate all phenomena as being devoid of intrinsic nature (niḥsvabhāva).
If one practices in this way, all vows will be fulfilled;
yet among these vows, one does not seek to attain the state of a Tathāgata or a Vajradhara.
I shall now further explain the mudrā-maṇḍala.
Within the altar, one should draw a vajra-sword;
at each of the four sides, according to its respective direction.
Draw the mudrās of the eight offerings and the four means of attraction (saṃgrahavastu).
By reciting [the mantra] before this maṇḍala,
accomplishment shall be attained before long.
I shall now further explain the Samaya Maṇḍala.
Within the altar, one should inscribe the five syllables and the seed-syllables of the eight offerings and the four means of attraction (saṃgrahavastu).
Facing this altar, while reciting the mantra, one should speak these words:
The syllable A-gate is that all phenomena are fundamentally unborn.
By reciting this daily,
before long all karmic obstacles will be extinguished and one will swiftly attain accomplishment.
I shall now further explain the Karma Maṇḍala.
Place a scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra within the altar,
and read, recite, and chant it every day.
One should worship them with various kinds of offerings,
and before long, success shall be achieved.
I shall now explain the method for painting the image.
Alternatively, one may paint Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva upon white cotton cloth, silk, or paper,
seated within a lunar disc.
Within the perimeter of the wheel, write five characters;
on the four sides, depict the eight offerings and the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*),
according to the ritual of the Great Maṇḍala.
Before this image, perform recitation according to the ritual rules and speak these words:
"The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is accomplished.
Recite this until the count reaches five hundred thousand times.
One will immediately attain inexhaustible eloquence,
no different from that of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva and others.
Soaring through the void, one shall achieve all sought-after worldly and world-transcending matters.
Furthermore, if one completes one koṭi of recitations,
one will be freed from all suffering and affliction;
if one completes two koṭis of repetitions, [the same result follows].
All karmic obstacles resulting from the five deeds of immediate retribution were forever exhausted without remainder;
after three koṭis of repetitions,
he realized all gateways to samādhi.
For forty million recitations, one attains great *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retention;
for fifty million recitations, one achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, regarding this method, [one should perform it] at the four sides of a *śarīra* stūpa.
Circumambulate clockwise while writing the five-syllable dhāraṇī;
walk around the stūpa reciting it without interruption until you have completed five lakṣas of repetitions.
At that time, the Tathāgata, Mañjuśrī, Vajrapāṇi, and the others manifested their bodies in the midst of space and continued to preach the Dharma for them.
I take refuge in the Youthful Mañjughoṣa; Relying upon Yoga, I shall explain the recitation.
With vajra mindfulness regarding the actions of body, speech, and mind,
The practitioner should give rise to the mind of Samantabhadra Through the profound gateway of the Tathāgata’s three secrets; Having received the vajra precepts from the master,
And giving no regard for body or life while arousing compassion, Only then may one be fit to enter the wheel of liberation.
One should receive the samaya from the master; the mudrās and secret mantras are as explained in the sūtras.
One should revere the ācārya with the thought that he is a Buddha, and maintain a heart of earnest devotion toward one’s fellow practitioners.
Whether in mountain retreats or *āraṇyakas*, by flowing springs, bathing pools, or beneath trees that bring delight—
At the edge of lofty trees by mountain peaks and stone caves, establish a maṇḍala according to the original rite;

adorn the inner sanctum and install the principal deity. Make offerings according to one's means and dwell with single-minded concentration, gazing universally upon the ocean of all Buddhas of the ten directions, making offerings and prostrating at the feet of all Tathāgatas.
In order to accomplish the vajra of the three activities, one should visualize five wisdom-vajras at the two hands, the tongue, and the heart.
Through this empowerment, all siddhis are attained;
next, one should form the mudrā called "Awakening," with both hands forming vajra-fists.
The thumb and ring finger hook together and point upward; the index fingers are held sideways to form the mudrā of awakening.
The mantra for awakening and alerting is as follows:
Homage to the Honored One Akṣobhya of the East! I offer my body and entreat you not to regress.

Prostrating with the entire body touching the ground, one pays homage with the mind. Joining the vajra palms and extending them above the crown of the head, one offers up the body and requests the empowerment of the mantra, saying:
"Next, one should respectfully prostrate to the Honored One Ratnasambhava, offering up the body and requesting the stage of empowerment."
With vajra-palms joined at the heart, one should touch the forehead to the ground and prostrate with devotion.
To request the empowerment, the mantra for surrendering the body is recited.
Next, one prostrates to the Lord Avalokiteśvara and surrenders the body to request samādhi.
Placing the vajra palms together upon the crown of the head, touch the mouth to the ground and with sincere devotion perform prostration;
the mantra for requesting samādhi by offering up one’s body is as follows.
Next, prostrate to the Honored One Amoghasiddhi and offer up one’s body to request skillful wisdom.
Placing the vajra-pañjali at the heart, touch the crown of the head to the ground and prostrate, making this request with the body surrendered.
The mantra for the skillful means is as follows:
Next, again pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions, visualizing one's own body pervading before all the Buddhas.
Visualize the five wheels touching the ground in prostration; one should then form the Vajrasamaya mudrā and recite the mantra for universally prostrating to the ten directions.
Next, recite the sublime mantra of accomplishment for the sake of all sentient beings who seek supreme success.
May all Tathāgatas grant their empowerment, swiftly causing me to accomplish the unsurpassed path and bring all sentient beings to maturity. The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should sit with legs crossed and body upright, purifying the three karmas until they are completely cleansed.
Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, may this body of mine be pure and stainless.
The mantra for purifying the three karmas is:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’ham. Then, with the vajra palms joined, interlace the first fingers of the ten digits and recite this mantra:
Oṃ vajrajāli jhaṭiti. Having formed the *vajrabandha* mudrā with the fists of all the *pāramitās*, recite this mantra:
Next, one should open the heart and enter the Buddha-wisdom. One should visualize two syllables, the letter *tra* and the letter *ṭha*, both white in color, at the two breasts;
these syllables should be visualized as two door-panels.
With both hands, one should form the vajra-bond; with three strikes at the heart, one opens the gateway.
The mantra for opening the heart-gate says:
"One should visualize the wondrous lotus as the letter-gateway A, and by means of the mudrā, summon [the deity] into the palace of the heart."
With concentration and wisdom as the moon, perform the vajra-bind. Visualize the syllables on the palms of the dhyāna and prajñā hands.
The mantra for entering the vajra is:
Next, one should form the seal for closing the door of the heart, using the same insignia as the seal for entering previously.
When the power of progress is exhausted, one abides in dhyāna and wisdom; immediately, one attains the firm, non-regressive Vajra-fist mantra.
Next, bind the Mañjuśrī-samaya mudrā: interlace the ten fingers to form a full moon.
Directly proclaiming the vajra-sword of patience and aspiration, one should visualize one’s own body as identical to Mañjuśrī.
The mantra of the Samaya is as follows:
Next, one should form the mudrā of the Joyful Samādhi; with the hands of concentration and wisdom, perform the firm binding of the moon.
The union of patience and the vow of deliverance, with generosity, wisdom, meditative concentration, and knowledge joined vertically,
is expressed by the mantra: Next,
bind the Vajra Trailokyavijaya mudrā and visualize one’s own body as being identical to it, without any distinction.
Forming the two vajra-fists of śamatha and vipaśyanā, hook the thumbs and little fingers together, extend the index and middle fingers,
and turn to the left to expel obstacles and bind the boundary to the right. To manifest the form of wrathful compassion,
the mantra of Trailokyavijaya is as follows:
Next, bind the Lotus Samaya mudrā for the sake of accomplishing contemplative practice (*vipaśyanā*).
Interlace the ten fingers to form a moon; join the *dhyāna* (middle) and *prajñā* (ring) fingers together vertically.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadmasamayas tvaṃ. The practitioner should practice the āsāphānaga rite.
One who cultivates this dharma remains motionless in their limbs and stops the inhalation and exhalation of breath,
making it subtle so that it does not become distracted.
One should then visualize all the Buddhas in the void,
filling the ten directions like sesame seeds;
with a vajra-snap of the fingers, they address the practitioner, saying:
"Good son, you should observe your original mind.
Having heard this, the practitioner immediately visualizes himself prostrating at the feet of all Buddhas.

When the ritual was concluded, he contemplated his fundamental mind with clarity and addressed the Buddhas, saying, "The characteristics of the mind have no substance; how, then, can it be cultivated and realized?
The Buddhas replied to the practitioner:
"Good son,
observe the moon-disc within your heart as if it were in a light mist,
and then recite the Mantra of the Luminous Bodhi."
The mantra for clearly contemplating the moon of the mind is:
Oṃ citta-prativedhaṃ karomi. The practitioner should clearly and attentively contemplate this.
Before long, you shall behold the pure bodhicitta,
free from all dust and defilements, as pure as the full moon.
Then, recite the mantra of bodhicitta:
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. One should visualize the syllable *daṃ* within the moon-disk of bodhicitta, radiant like the color of gold.
Like the sun emitting great radiance,
it immediately transforms into the sword of the Prajñāpāramitā;
free from all conceptual discrimination, it is able to sever the afflictions.
The mantra for visualizing the sword of wisdom is:
Oṃ tiṣṭha khaḍga. One should visualize that the sword of wisdom gradually increases in size until it pervades the entire dharmadhātu. The mantra is: [Oṃ tiṣṭha khaḍga].
Oṃ saṃsphāra-krodha. One should visualize the wisdom sword gradually withdrawing [the emanations] until it is equal in size to one's own body. The mantra is:
Oṃ saṃhara-krodha. To make the wisdom sword firm and prevent its dispersal, recite the mantra again:
Oṃ nṛtyatiṣṭha kha-ga. Visualize that all Tathāgatas enter the space of the wisdom-sword and become a single entity.
Contemplate in this manner.
"Just as the essential nature of those Buddhas is such, so too am I. The mantra is:
*Oṃ samayam ahaṃ samayas tvaṃ sarvatathāgatājñādhipate mañjughoṣa*. Visualize that the sword of wisdom gradually transforms into the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
Possessing great majesty and virtue, his body is adorned with various kinds of necklaces;
imagine five topknots upon his head,
and his right hand holds the sword of wisdom.
Her left hand holds a blue lotus flower,
upon which rests a case containing the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
her body is the color of saffron.
Recite "A-ra-pa-ca-na" once mentally. Next, form the Vajrajñānakhaḍga-mudrā:
interlace the thumbs and ring fingers in the manner of śamatha and vipaśyanā, and extend the index and little fingers upright like the shape of a sword.
Seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head.
The mantra for the firm fundamental deity that immediately accomplishes the protection of the body is as follows:
Next, one should perform the consecration by forming the Jewel Mudrā: interlace the two hands to form the crescent moon;
extend the index fingers (vajra-angulī) and bend them back like the shape of a jewel; then, join the tips of the ring fingers and the little fingers together.
Place it upon the forehead and divide it into two sides; then form the *jñānamuṣṭi* (wisdom-fist) as if tying a silk ribbon.
With both hands extended forward, slowly release them. One should know that the stainless silken cloth has now been tied.
The mantra is: [Mantra follows]
Next, perform the mudrā of the Precious Sword for self-consecration:
join the two palms, bend the index fingers (vajra-fingers) and the middle fingers (wisdom-fingers), and tuck both into the palms. Place this at the forehead and divide it to both sides.
The mantra for consecration is as follows:
Next, again bind the Armor Mudrā: form vajra-fists with both hands and place them before the heart;
extend the two *tarjanīs* (forefingers). Visualize the syllable Oṃ at each of the two [fingers], imagining that clear light flows forth as green in color.
Perform three circumambulations around the heart and behind the back.
Again, it reaches below the navel and both knees; then it moves back to the navel, circles behind the waist, and from the waist proceeds to the heart, circling the two shoulders.
From the shoulders it goes to the throat, toward the back of the neck, and again from the back of the neck to the front of the forehead.
From the forehead it reaches the brain, where one forms the *jñāna-muṣṭi* (wisdom-fist).

Gradually dispersing downward like hanging ribbons, looking upward at the rotation as if in a dancing posture, the two hands interlace to form the full-moon gesture. The mantra for the armor is as follows:
Next, perform the ritual of the vajra-clapping of the palms; with both wings [hands] clapping together, they strike once.
By reciting the *Cenchapa* mantra, one causes the assembly of noble ones to rejoice and swiftly attains the firm body of the deity. The mantra for rejoicing is as follows:
Next, the practitioner should visualize an eight-petaled lotus with filaments and anthers before their seat.
Above, one contemplates the wondrous lion throne of Mount Meru;
upon the throne, within a pavilion of the seven treasures, one visualizes a sovereign lotus flower made of the seven treasures.
Above that, one visualizes the syllable *tām*, endowed with majestic radiance, which illuminates the entire Dharma-realm without exception; this syllable transforms into a sharp vajra.
Clearly and attentively visualize [the deity] in its original form. Summon the Bodhisattva to enter the visualized body;
with both hands forming the moon-advancing hook (*candrāṅkuśa*), visualize the body as being identical to that Bodhisattva.
The mantra of the Vajrāṅkuśa Bodhisattva is as follows:
Next, one should bind the cord and enter the body of the Honored One.

By binding the *candra-dhyāna* and pressing the wisdom [hand] into the palm, through the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of this secret seal (*mudrā*), they are transformed into a single entity without distinction.
The mantra of the Vajrapāśa is as follows:
Next, one should perform the Locking Seal (Śṛṅkhalā-mudrā) to make [the bonds] firm;
performing it four times each month like a ring, by the power of this secret seal, all shall be made firm and unchanging.
The Vajra-Śṛṅkhalā Mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the bell mudrā to bring forth joy: with the thumbs and wisdom fingers joined like a bell, cause the Honored One and the assembly to rejoice.
The mantra for the vajra bell, which empowers it for swift and wondrous accomplishment, is as follows:
Oṃ khaṇḍa akha akha. Next, the practitioner should hold arghya water with both hands and imagine washing the feet of the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśī and her retinue;
or else, empower the arghya water with the hundred-syllable mantra.
Then, recite the Ekajaṭā mantra.
Next, form the Mañju-karma-mudrā: with both hands forming vajra-fists, place the left hand (the dhyāna-hand) upon one's own heart, while the right hand maintains the posture of grasping a sword.
By the power of this excellent seal of the rite, the body attains equality with the Honored One, without distinction.
The rite mantra is as follows:
Next, bind the seal of the Vajra Sharp Sword; join the moon-seal (the *samaya-mudrā*) and extend the *amogha* fingers like a sword.
By means of this adamantine, sharp, and wondrous seal, one shall attain the profound wisdom of Prajñā.
The Adamantine Sharp Mantra is as follows:
Next, one should perform the inner offering; forming the moon-seal at the heart, one should extend the dhyāna and prajñā fingers upward.
By binding the Vajralāsyā mudrā, one swiftly fulfills the dānapāramitā.
The mantra of Vajralāsyā is as follows:
Next, perform the offering with the Vajramālā; following the previous lāsyā gesture, extend the arms straight out.
By the empowerment of binding this mudrā, one shall fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā).
The mantra of the Vajramālā is as follows.
Next, bind the Vajragīta mudrā; let the garland hang down from the navel to the mouth and then disperse it.
By forming the secret mudrā of the Vajra Song, one swiftly attains the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).
The mantra of the Vajra Song is as follows:
Next, perform the offering of the Vajra Dance; with both hands in fists, rotate them in the manner of a dance.
By means of the empowerment of the Vajra Dance mudrā, one swiftly fulfills the perfection of diligence.
The mantra of the Vajra Dance mudrā is as follows:
Next, perform the outer vajra offering; with both hands, form the moon-gesture and scatter it downward.
By the power of binding the incense-offering mudrā, one shall realize the Vajra Incense Mantra of the Dhyāna-pāramitā.
Next, bind the Vajra Flower-scattering Mudrā; form the moon [mudrā] facing upward as if scattering flowers.
Through the empowerment of this Flower-Scattering Mudrā, one swiftly realizes Prajñāpāramitā.
The Vajra Flower-Scattering Mantra is as follows:
Next, form the Vajra Lamp Illumination Mudrā, joining the tips of the moon-like dhyāna and wisdom fingers.
By forming the Vajra-Light-Embellishment Mudrā, one shall attain the Vajra-Light Mantra of the Skillful Means Pāramitā. It is said:
Next, form the Vajra-Perfume Mudrā; with the left hand at the chest, scatter [the fingers] like spreading perfume.
By empowering with the mudrā of the incense offering, one swiftly fulfills the perfection of the vow.
The Vajra Incense Mantra is:
Oṃ sugandhe svāhā. Following this, the practitioner should recite the One Hundred and Eight Names as a praise and make offerings to the tutelary deity.
Furthermore, having bound the Vajra Sharp Sword mudrā and empowered oneself by reciting the hundred-syllable mantra at the heart,
even if one has committed various evil karmas in past lives, such as the five crimes of immediate retribution and all other obstacles of transgression—
By virtue of the empowerment of this hundred-syllable mantra,
all karmic obstacles and transgressions are completely extinguished,
and one beholds the body attaining the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
If the mind is distracted, one should recite this vidyā seven times, twenty-one times, thirty-seven times, up to seven times seventy or one hundred and eight times;
the mind will then be freed from discursive attachments and swiftly attain samādhi.
The Hundred-Syllable Mantra: Oṃ kha ga sa tva sa ma ya ma nu pa la ya kha ga sa tva ti ve nu pa ti ṣṭha ni rju ta miṅ ba su sto.
Siṃhayūthamiva 6. Aṇaraktumiva 7.
Supuṣpamiva 8. Sarvasiddhiprāyaśca 9. Sarvakarmasvaccha 10. Jñātṛśīla.
Hrīḥ jñānakūru hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ svābhāvaṃ sarvatathāgatāgryamūrdhajñaḥ khaṅgiṅkhabhava mahāsamayasattvāya phaṭ.
Sixth, without releasing the previous mudrā,
gaze intently at the principal deity before you and imagine yourself as being no different from that deity.
Observe clearly and recite the five-syllable dhāraṇī;
recite it either with adamantine speech or with distinct lotus-like speech.
Recite seven times, or twenty-one times.
Release the seal at the crown of the head.
Then, holding the rosary at the heart, recite with a pace that is neither too slow nor too fast.
Recite either one hundred and eight times, one thousand times, or even ten thousand times.
When the count of recitations is complete,
hold the rosary with both hands and place it upon the crown of your head.
Thereafter, place it back in its original location.
If one performs recitation through meditative absorption (samādhi),
one should visualize the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom within the mind.
In the center, arrange the five syllable-gates;
contemplate them clearly and with precision,
ensuring they correspond to their respective meanings.
When the mind is united with the Prajñāpāramitā,
this is called the recitation of samādhi.
If the body becomes weary, [one should rest].
Then, form the mudrā of the Vajra-sword of the Honored One and recite the five-syllable dhāraṇī seven times.
Furthermore, offer the eight great offerings to all the Buddhas.
Praise and extol with sublime sounds and words;
offer arghya water;
and dissolve the boundary by turning the traidhātuka mudrā counter-clockwise.
Then, forming the Vajra Sharp Sword mudrā,
one respectfully escorts all the holy ones back to their respective original palaces.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kṛtva sarvasattvarātra siddhyanta athānujñā gaccha dharmaviśaye punarāgaccha mānaṃ te 'stu. Oṃ kaga sattvamukha. Having performed this rite, [the mantra is recited].
Furthermore, having empowered with the mantra while reciting it with the samaya-mudrā and sealing the four places [of the body] with that mudrā,
one then performs the empowerment and dons the vajra armor.
Perform the fourfold prostrations to the Buddhas of the four directions,
engage in repentance, make vows, and so forth;
thereafter, rely upon a secluded and tranquil place.
Adorned with incense and flowers, abide in the samādhi of the deity and recite all Mahāyāna sūtras of the Vaipulya class,
such as the Great Prajñāpāramitā in Twenty-five Thousand Lines and the Mañjuśrī-prajñāpāramitā, and so forth.
Walk at will. If a wise person relies on this Dharma, practicing with diligence throughout the four periods of day and night,
they shall realize the Stage of Joy (Prāmodyabhūmi) in this very life and attain perfect enlightenment after sixteen future lifetimes.
The Mañjuśrī-krodha-dhāraṇī: Oṃ vajratīkṣṇa kuru dhīna dhīna hūṃ phaṭ. Use this mantra to protect the body, expel obstructors, and establish the boundary.
One may also obtain purified incense, flowers, and all other ritual implements.

At that time, one should make this aspiration for all sentient beings: May they encounter these teachings, May Mañjuśrī always be their spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), And may they swiftly realize the skillful wisdom of *prajñā*, Quickly attaining the state of the Unsurpassed Honored One among Two-Legged Beings.

The Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī: *A-ra-pa-ca-na* (Arapacana). *Oṃ vajratikṣṇa oṃ nukha-ce oṃ kaga-gara khaṃ oṃ kaga-sattva*. From the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, the Yoga Section, Chapter One: The Dharma of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
